lines.text: Where do you hide the most wanted man on Earth?
Not in a cave — behind a fourteen-foot wall, in a quiet army town.
For six years, Osama bin Laden lived in Abbottabad, near a military academy.
No phones, no internet, trash burned in the yard. And the CIA noticed.
Just after midnight, May second, twenty eleven — Operation Neptune Spear was a go.
Twenty-three SEALs, an interpreter, and a combat dog.
A hundred and twenty miles from Afghanistan, in two stealth Black Hawks.
As they came in low, the CIA cut the neighborhood's power.
The SEALs swept in on night vision.
And the first Black Hawk slammed into the dirt.
No one was hurt. The mission kept going.
Forty minutes after it began, bin Laden was dead, on the third floor.
They took his files, blew up the wreck, and vanished before sunrise.
Ten years of hiding from armies and satellites — found living in plain sight.
The only proof of that night is a hole, where a helicopter used to be.
